card.statement:
For each system of linear
and semilinear mappings <<ref:jsttw>>,
there exist bases of the spaces
$V_1,\dots,V_t$ in which the sequence
of matrices of
${\cal{A}}_{1},\dots,{\cal{A}}_{t}$ is
a direct sum, determined by
<<ref:jsttw>> uniquely up to
permutation of summands, of sequences
of the following form $($in which the
points denote sequences of identity
matrices or $0_{00})$:

- [(i)]

- [$\bullet$]
$(J_n(\lambda),\ldots)$ in
which $\lambda\ne 0$, if
the number of dashed arrows
in <<ref:jsttw>> is even,

- [$\bullet$]
$(J_n(\lambda),\ldots)$ and
$(H_{2k}(\mu),\ldots)$ in
which $\lambda $ is real
and positive and $\mu $
is either not real or is
real and negative, if the
number of dashed arrows in
<<ref:jsttw>> is odd;

- [(ii)] $(\ldots, J_n(0),
    \ldots)$ with $J_n(0)$ at
position $i\in \{1,\ldots,
    t\}$;

- [(iii)] $(\ldots,
    A_i,\ldots, A_j,\ldots)$ in
which

- [$\bullet$]
$(A_i,A_j)=(F_n,G_n)$ or
$(F_n^T,G_n^T)$ if ${\cal
      A}_i$ and ${\cal
A}_j$ have opposite directions
in

\begin{equation}
V_1\li{{\cal A}_1}
V_2\li{{\cal A}_2}  \cdots
\li{{\cal A}_{t-1}}
V_t\li{{\cal A}_t} V_1
\end{equation}

- [$\bullet$] $(A_i,A_j)=
      (F_n,G_n^T)$ or
$(F_n^T,G_n)$ if ${\cal
      A}_i$ and ${\cal A}_j$
have the same direction in
<<ref:1.6>>.
card.label: Theorem 1.1

paper.title: Cycles of linear and semilinear mappings
paper.abstract: We give a canonical form of matrices of a cycle of linear or semilinear mapping V_1 --- V_2 --- ... --- V_t --- V_1 in which all V_i are complex vector spaces, each line is an arrow ---> or <---, and each arrow denotes a linear or semilinear mapping.
